item.title: Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins wins race for Alaska governor, replaces a Republican
item.description: Kreiss-Tomkins, a former state legislator, ran a campaign emphasizing bipartisanship in the the state that usually votes Republican. At 37, he'll be the youngest governor in the state's history.

item.title: DHS head Markwayne Mullin says there is not a threat to the U.S. amid FAA ground stop
item.description: Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin spoke to at the White House on Friday afternoon after the FAA issues a total ground stop. NPR was there for the briefing.

item.title: Stuck on the tarmac without information: Travelers share their ground stop experiences
item.description: Passengers stuck on airplanes on tarmacs across the country during the FAA ground stop on Friday share their stories.
item.content:encoded: Passengers stuck on airplanes on tarmacs across the country during the FAA ground stop on Friday share their stories.

item.title: What we know about the FAA nationwide ground stop
item.description: The Federal Aviation Administration took an extraordinary step Friday afternoon by issuing a nationwide ground stop. No planes are taking off at any airport and millions of passengers are stranded.
item.content:encoded: The Federal Aviation Administration took an extraordinary step Friday afternoon by issuing a nationwide ground stop. No planes are taking off at any airport and millions of passengers are stranded.
item.dc:creator: Joel Rose

item.title: GOP state officials push to revive Trump's mail voting restrictions for 2028 election
item.description: Some Republican state officials are reviving a bid for mail-in voting restrictions for the 2028 election by appealing a court order blocking the Postal Service from carrying out a revised ballot rule.

item.title: With his challenge to Schumer, Van Hollen forces a debate over Democrats' mandate
item.description: Democrats say they have a mandate to deliver change, but as the party gets ready to retake the majority in both the House and Senate, there are divides over who should lead it.

item.title: The government says it will close a beloved D.C. park Sunday. Will a judge step in?
item.description: Federal judge Ana Reyes grilled the government on Friday about its plans for East Potomac Park, and indicated she could order it to remain open despite President Trump's renovation wishes.

item.title: What's Trump's strategy now with Iran? To keep things as they are
item.description: President Trump says the "status quo" is what Gulf Arab allies want as the Iran war hits a stalemate and the U.S. midterms force a pivot from threats of attacks to economic pressure.
